result:
The community's decision isn't recorded in any commit message or ticket I could reach, so the conditions-list rule below is inferred from the code change. The commit that made it has an empty body.

**What the conditions list shows now.** `useConditions` queries FHIR `Condition` filtered to the `problem-list-item` category, so only the problem list appears there (commit `64d3c99`, "Filter conditions query to problem-list-item category (#3403)", by Nethmi Rodrigo). The same commit raised the fhir2 requirement in the conditions `routes.json` to `>=2.8.0`. On the backend, `problem-list-item` maps to a Condition and `encounter-diagnosis` maps to a Diagnosis (`FhirUtils.java`). So visit-note diagnoses are encounter diagnoses, and they are meant to appear under the visit rather than in the conditions list.

**What else had to change so diagnoses still show with the right visit.** Visit diagnoses are gathered across all encounters of a visit, so the same diagnosis could appear several times. Commit `1a2af77` (O3-5822, "Dedupe diagnoses in visit-level rollups") added `dedupeDiagnoses`, which sorts by rank (primary first) and keeps one entry per concept UUID or non-coded text. It is used in the visit history diagnosis cell and in the visit summary.

**Why it needed a reload (from reading the code, not a recorded bug).** After a visit note is saved, the form invalidates visit and encounter caches only. `invalidatePatientEncounters` matches keys containing `/encounter`, and the conditions `Condition?patient=` key is not touched, so the conditions list stays stale until reload. I found no commit that adds a conditions revalidation here.

**Ticket caveat.** O3-5822 is the only ticket I found that fits the visit-level diagnosis work. Nothing links it to the conditions-filter commit, so treat it as the likely ticket rather than a confirmed one.

Paths below are under `openmrs-esm-patient-chart` unless noted. The `openmrs-module-fhir2` lines are from a partial read of `FhirUtils.java`.

- `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-conditions-app/src/conditions/conditions.resource.ts:129-135` — `useConditions` with the problem-list-item category filter.
- `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-conditions-app/src/conditions/conditions-widget.component.tsx:73` — the conditions widget's `useConditions` and `mutate`.
- `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/dedupe-diagnoses.ts:1-24` — `dedupeDiagnoses`.
- `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visit-history-table/visit-diagnoses-cell.component.tsx:8-16` — visit history diagnosis cell using the dedupe.
- `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visits-widget/past-visits-components/visit-summary.component.tsx:86-94` — visit summary using the dedupe.
- `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/visit/revalidation-utils.ts:76-82` — `invalidatePatientEncounters`, which does not cover the Condition key.
- `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-notes-app/src/notes/visit-notes-form.component.tsx:516-524` — post-save invalidation in the visit note form.
- `openmrs-module-fhir2/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/fhir2/api/util/FhirUtils.java:152-179` — category to Condition/Diagnosis mapping.
- `openmrs-module-fhir2/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/fhir2/api/impl/FhirConditionServiceImpl.java:93` — accepted categories: problem-list-item or encounter-diagnosis.

The trigger's accessible name comes from iconDescription, which defaults to 'Options'. Every overflow menu in this repo passed its label via aria-label, so screen readers announced a generic 'Options' for all of them.\n\nPass the label through iconDescription instead in the visit timeline, encounters table, orders and medications tables, and the allergies, conditions, procedures, programs, and vitals action menus. The conditions menu label was a hardcoded string, so it is now translated. Unit tests and e2e specs that located the triggers by the 'Options' name now use the real labels.\n\n* Keep aria-label on overflow menus so the popup stays named\n\nCarbon's classic OverflowMenu applies aria-label to the opened menu body (the ul with role menu), so dropping it left the popup without an accessible name. Keep aria-label alongside iconDescription so the trigger and the popup are both named. The encounters table test now asserts the popup's aria-label.\n\n* Disambiguate the delete confirmation locators in the e2e specs\n\nThe allergies, biometrics, and vitals trigger names now contain the word delete, so the modal confirmation locator getByRole('button', { name: /delete/i }) matched two elements and failed in strict mode. Target the modal's danger button instead, matching the existing conditions spec.\n\n* Cover the remaining overflow menu labels\n\nName the procedures, attachment preview, and clinical encounter list menus consistently. Remove the misplaced attachment menu item label and cover the accessible names in focused tests.\n\n* Update the procedures and attachments e2e locators for the new trigger names\n\nThe procedures and attachment preview triggers are now named 'Edit or delete procedure' and 'Attachment actions', so the specs can no longer find them by 'Options'.","authorName":"Dennis Kigen","authorEmail":"kigen.work@gmail.com"},{"hash":"64d3c9902168b1a43b08d5da09558e7da6288a0d","date":"2026-06-19T18:51:12+05:30","message":"(fix) Filter conditions query to problem-list-item category (#3403)","refs":"","body":"","authorName":"Nethmi Rodrigo","authorEmail":"nethmi@openmrs.org"},{"hash":"bd0350391135e8e0cb8ac61cabd0e3ce5256b28d","date":"2026-06-09T16:10:29+03:00","message":"(fix) O3-5709: Change the conditions left-nav icon to distinguish it from the task list (#3359)","refs":"","body":"fix(O3-5709): use table-of-contents icon for Conditions to distinguish from task list\n\nThe Conditions item in the patient chart's left nav and the Task list in\nthe right rail both rendered omrs-icon-list-checked, falsely implying a\nsemantic link between a longitudinal clinical problem list and operational\naction items.\n\nSwitch Conditions to omrs-icon-table-of-contents, an already-registered,\nunclaimed glyph that reads as a list without the checklist connotation. 1: import type { KeyedMutator } from 'swr';
2: import { restBaseUrl } from '@openmrs/esm-framework';
3: 
4: /**
5:  * Invalidates visit history table data without triggering global visit revalidation cascade.
6:  *
7:  * This function provides surgical SWR cache invalidation for visit operations. It targets only
8:  * the paginated visit data used by the visit history table, avoiding unnecessary revalidation
9:  * of the 28+ components that use current visit data via the useVisit hook.
10:  *
11:  * The implementation uses URL pattern matching to discriminate between:
12:  * - Current visit keys (includeInactive=false) - these are NOT invalidated
13:  * - Visit history keys (no includeInactive param, or pagination params) - these ARE invalidated
14:  *
15:  * Cache key patterns:
16:  * - Current visit: /visit?patient=123&v=custom&includeInactive=false
17:  * - Visit history: /visit?patient=123&v=custom:(uuid,location...)&limit=10&startIndex=0&totalCount=true
18:  *
19:  * This approach eliminates the 13+ cascade revalidation requests that were previously triggered
20:  * by global mutateVisit() calls, reducing network traffic and improving performance.
21:  *
22:  * @param mutate - SWR mutate function from useSWRConfig()
23:  * @param patientUuid - Patient UUID to target visit data for
24:  *
25:  * @example
26:  * ```typescript
27:  * import { useSWRConfig } from 'swr';
28:  * import { invalidateVisitHistory } from '@openmrs/esm-patient-common-lib';
29:  *
30:  * function MyComponent({ patientUuid }) {
31:  *   const { mutate } = useSWRConfig();
32:  *
33:  *   const handleVisitUpdate = async () => {
34:  *     // Perform visit operation...
35:  *     await updateVisit(visitData);
36:  *
37:  *     // Invalidate only visit history table, not current visit components
38:  *     invalidateVisitHistory(mutate, patientUuid);
39:  *   };
40:  * }
41:  * ```
42:  */
43: export function invalidateVisitHistory(mutate: KeyedMutator<unknown>, patientUuid: string): void {
44:   mutate((key) => {
45:     if (typeof key === 'string' && key.includes(`${restBaseUrl}/visit?patient=${patientUuid}`)) {
46:       // Current visit keys have includeInactive=false
47:       const isCurrentVisitKey = key.includes('includeInactive=false');
48: 
49:       // Visit history keys typically have pagination parameters or no includeInactive parameter
50:       const hasHistoryParams = key.includes('limit=') || key.includes('startIndex=') || key.includes('totalCount=');
51:       const hasNoIncludeInactive = !key.includes('includeInactive');
52: 
53:       // Invalidate if it's clearly a history key OR if it doesn't have includeInactive=false
54:       // This ensures we target visit history while preserving current visit cache
55:       return !isCurrentVisitKey && (hasHistoryParams || hasNoIncludeInactive);
56:     }
57:     return false;
58:   });
59: }
60: 
61: /**
62:  * Invalidates visit-related encounter data for a specific patient.
63:  *
64:  * This function is useful when operations create or modify encounters within visits,
65:  * requiring the encounter lists and related data to be refreshed.
66:  *
67:  * @param mutate - SWR mutate function from useSWRConfig()
68:  * @param patientUuid - Patient UUID to target encounter data for
69:  *
70:  * @example
71:  * ```typescript
72:  * // After creating a visit note (which creates an encounter)
73:  * invalidatePatientEncounters(mutate, patientUuid);
74:  * ```
75:  */
76: export function invalidatePatientEncounters(mutate: KeyedMutator<unknown>, patientUuid: string): void {
77:   mutate((key) => {
78:     return (
79:       typeof key === 'string' && key.includes(`${restBaseUrl}/encounter`) && key.includes(`patient=${patientUuid}`)
80:     );
81:   });
82: }
83: 
84: /**
85:  * Invalidates only the current (active) visit cache for a specific patient.
86:  *

+import { type Diagnosis } from '@openmrs/esm-framework';
+
+/**
+ * Sorts diagnoses by rank (primary first) and collapses repeats of the same diagnosis
+ * recorded across multiple encounters of a visit into a single entry, keeping the
+ * highest-ranked occurrence. Coded diagnoses are keyed by concept UUID and non-coded
+ * diagnoses by their text.
+ */
+export function dedupeDiagnoses(diagnoses: Array<Diagnosis>): Array<Diagnosis> {
+  const seen = new Set<string>();
+  return [...diagnoses]
+    .sort((a, b) => a.rank - b.rank)
+    .filter((diagnosis) => {
+      const key = diagnosis.diagnosis?.coded?.uuid ?? diagnosis.diagnosis?.nonCoded;
+      if (!key) {
+        return true;
+      }
+      if (seen.has(key)) {
+        return false;
+      }
+      seen.add(key);
+      return true;
+    });
+}

+import { type Diagnosis } from '@openmrs/esm-framework';
+
+/**
+ * Sorts diagnoses by rank (primary first) and collapses repeats of the same diagnosis
+ * recorded across multiple encounters of a visit into a single entry, keeping the
+ * highest-ranked occurrence. Coded diagnoses are keyed by concept UUID and non-coded
+ * diagnoses by their text.
+ */
+export function dedupeDiagnoses(diagnoses: Array<Diagnosis>): Array<Diagnosis> {
+  const seen = new Set<string>();
+  return [...diagnoses]
+    .sort((a, b) => a.rank - b.rank)
+    .filter((diagnosis) => {
+      const key = diagnosis.diagnosis?.coded?.uuid ?? diagnosis.diagnosis?.nonCoded;
+      if (!key) {
+        return true;
+      }
+      if (seen.has(key)) {
+        return false;
+      }
+      seen.add(key);
+      return true;
+    });
+}
